questions.question: For the linear program $\max Z=\boldsymbol{c}^{\top}\boldsymbol{x}$, $\boldsymbol{A}\boldsymbol{x}=\boldsymbol{b}$, $\boldsymbol{x}\geq\boldsymbol{0}$ with current basis matrix $\boldsymbol{B}$, which quantities does one iteration of the revised simplex algorithm compute?
options: The whole table $\boldsymbol{B}^{-1}\boldsymbol{A}$ with its objective row, obtained from the previous tableau by one pivot
The reduced costs and the columns $\boldsymbol{B}^{-1}\boldsymbol{A}_j$ of all nonbasic variables, to compare every exchange
The reduced costs of the nonbasic variables, one pivot column and the right-hand side $\boldsymbol{B}^{-1}\boldsymbol{b}$
Only the reduced costs, since the right-hand side $\boldsymbol{B}^{-1}\boldsymbol{b}$ stays the same from basis to basis

questions.question: A linear program $\max Z=\boldsymbol{c}^{\top}\boldsymbol{x}$ with $m$ constraints $\leq\boldsymbol{b}$ and $\boldsymbol{x}\geq\boldsymbol{0}$ is written in equation form with $m$ slack variables. When is the slack basis, with $\boldsymbol{B}=\boldsymbol{I}_m$, a valid start for step 1 of the revised simplex algorithm?
options: Always, since $\boldsymbol{B}=\boldsymbol{I}_m$ is invertible and therefore defines a basis
Only when $\boldsymbol{b}>\boldsymbol{0}$ strictly, since a basic variable equal to $0$ is not allowed
Only when the linear program is bounded, since otherwise no basic feasible solution exists
When $\boldsymbol{b}\geq\boldsymbol{0}$, so that $\boldsymbol{x}_{\mathcal{B}}=\boldsymbol{b}$ is feasible

questions.question: The tableau version of the simplex algorithm computes each tableau from the previous one, so rounding errors are carried along. Why does the revised simplex algorithm not carry errors over from one tableau to the next in this way?
options: It works with exact fractions throughout, so that no rounding happens at all
It computes every quantity afresh from the original data and the current $\boldsymbol{B}^{-1}$
It updates the objective row from the previous objective row, which stays exact
It always pivots on the largest entry of the pivot column to keep errors small

questions.question: With the same rules for breaking ties, how do the bases visited by the revised simplex algorithm compare with those visited by the tableau version of the simplex method?
options: Fewer bases, since it prices out only the nonbasic columns in each iteration
Different bases, since computing from the original data changes the choices
The same bases, so it can also cycle, and Bland's rule repairs it likewise
The same bases, but it cannot cycle, since $\boldsymbol{B}^{-1}$ is recomputed each time

questions.question: For $\max Z=4x_1+3x_2+5x_3$ in equation form with slacks $x_4,x_5,x_6$ (objective coefficient $0$), the revised simplex algorithm has the basis $(x_3,x_5,x_2)$ in this order. The entering variable $x_1$ wins the minimum-ratio test in position $k^*=2$. Which $\boldsymbol{c}_{\mathcal{B}}$ goes with the updated $\boldsymbol{B}^{-1}$ in the next step 2?
options: $\boldsymbol{c}_{\mathcal{B}}=(4,3,5)^{\top}$
$\boldsymbol{c}_{\mathcal{B}}=(5,4,3)^{\top}$
$\boldsymbol{c}_{\mathcal{B}}=(5,3,4)^{\top}$
$\boldsymbol{c}_{\mathcal{B}}=(5,0,3)^{\top}$

questions.question: At a basic feasible solution of $\max Z=\boldsymbol{c}^{\top}\boldsymbol{x}$, the nonbasic reduced costs $\bar{c}_j=-c_j+\boldsymbol{c}_{\mathcal{B}}^{\top}\boldsymbol{B}^{-1}\boldsymbol{A}_j$ are $\bar{c}_1=4$, $\bar{c}_3=-2$, $\bar{c}_5=-\frac{5}{2}$ and $\bar{c}_6=0$. Which variable enters under the rule that picks the most negative reduced cost?

In step 4 of the revised simplex algorithm, the basis is $(x_4,x_2,x_6)$ in this order, $\boldsymbol{B}^{-1}\boldsymbol{b}=(6,2,9)^{\top}$, and the entering variable $x_3$ has pivot column $\boldsymbol{B}^{-1}\boldsymbol{A}_3=(3,-1,2)^{\top}$. Which variable leaves the basis?

In step 6 of the revised simplex algorithm the basis is $(x_3,x_1)$ in this order, with $\boldsymbol{B}^{-1}=\begin{bmatrix}\frac{3}{4}&-\frac{1}{2}\\-\frac{1}{4}&\frac{1}{2}\end{bmatrix}$ and $\boldsymbol{b}=(6,7)^{\top}$. Which values does $\boldsymbol{x}_{\mathcal{B}}=\boldsymbol{B}^{-1}\boldsymbol{b}$ give to the basic variables?

In step 4 of the revised simplex algorithm, the basis is $(x_2,x_4,x_5)$ in this order, $\boldsymbol{B}^{-1}\boldsymbol{b}=(4,6,5)^{\top}$, and the entering variable $x_1$ has pivot column $\boldsymbol{B}^{-1}\boldsymbol{A}_1=(2,3,1)^{\top}$. The minimum-ratio test lets $x_2$ leave. What are the values of the basic variables $x_1,x_4,x_5$ after the exchange?

In step 2 of the revised simplex algorithm, why is it convenient to compute the row vector $\boldsymbol{c}_{\mathcal{B}}^{\top}\boldsymbol{B}^{-1}$ first and then $\bar{c}_j=-c_j+(\boldsymbol{c}_{\mathcal{B}}^{\top}\boldsymbol{B}^{-1})\boldsymbol{A}_j$ for each nonbasic $j$?
options: Each reduced cost then needs one product with $\boldsymbol{A}_j$, instead of $\boldsymbol{B}^{-1}\boldsymbol{A}_j$ for every $j$
Its entries are the reduced costs of the structural variables, which saves pricing them out
The other grouping, $\boldsymbol{c}_{\mathcal{B}}^{\top}(\boldsymbol{B}^{-1}\boldsymbol{A}_j)$, would give a different and wrong value
It equals the objective value $Z$ of the current basic feasible solution

questions.question: In step 5 of the revised simplex algorithm, at an arbitrary current basis (not only the slack basis), $x_{j^*}$ enters in position $k^*$ of the basis. How can the new $\boldsymbol{B}^{-1}$ be obtained from the old one without inverting the new basis matrix?
options: Replace column $k^*$ of the old $\boldsymbol{B}^{-1}$ by the pivot column $\boldsymbol{B}^{-1}\boldsymbol{A}_{j^*}$
Apply to the old $\boldsymbol{B}^{-1}$ the row operations that turn $\boldsymbol{B}^{-1}\boldsymbol{A}_{j^*}$ into $\boldsymbol{e}_{k^*}$
Change only row $k^*$ of the old $\boldsymbol{B}^{-1}$, since only column $k^*$ of $\boldsymbol{B}$ changes
Apply to the old $\boldsymbol{B}^{-1}$ the row operations that turn the original $\boldsymbol{A}_{j^*}$ into $\boldsymbol{e}_{k^*}$

questions.question: In an iteration of the revised simplex algorithm for $\max Z=\boldsymbol{c}^{\top}\boldsymbol{x}$, the entering variable has reduced cost $\bar{c}_{j^*}=-2$ and the minimum ratio is $\theta=0$, because the leaving basic variable already equals $0$. What does this exchange do?
options: It raises $Z$ by $2$, since every entering variable with $\bar{c}_{j^*}<0$ improves $Z$
It shows that the program is unbounded, since no basic variable limits $x_{j^*}$
It is not allowed: with $\theta=0$ the next negative reduced cost must be tried
It changes the basis, but the basic solution and the value of $Z$ stay the same

questions.question: In the revised simplex algorithm the basis is $(x_4,x_2)$ in this order, with $\boldsymbol{B}^{-1}=\begin{bmatrix}1&-\frac{1}{3}\\0&\frac{1}{3}\end{bmatrix}$ and $\boldsymbol{x}_{\mathcal{B}}=(4,4)^{\top}$. The entering variable $x_3$ has pivot column $\boldsymbol{B}^{-1}\boldsymbol{A}_3=(\frac{5}{3},\frac{1}{3})^{\top}$. What is $\boldsymbol{B}^{-1}$ after the exchange?
options: $\begin{bmatrix}\frac{3}{5}&-\frac{1}{5}\\\frac{1}{5}&\frac{4}{15}\end{bmatrix}$
$\begin{bmatrix}1&-2\\0&1\end{bmatrix}$
$\begin{bmatrix}\frac{3}{5}&-\frac{1}{5}\\-\frac{1}{5}&\frac{2}{5}\end{bmatrix}$
$\begin{bmatrix}\frac{3}{5}&-\frac{1}{5}\\-\frac{1}{3}&\frac{4}{9}\end{bmatrix}$

questions.question: In the revised simplex algorithm the basis is $(x_1,x_5,x_6)$ in this order, with $\boldsymbol{B}^{-1}=\begin{bmatrix}1&0&0\\-2&1&0\\-3&0&1\end{bmatrix}$ and $\boldsymbol{x}_{\mathcal{B}}=(2,5,3)^{\top}$. The entering variable $x_3$ has column $\boldsymbol{A}_3=(1,1,4)^{\top}$ in the original constraint matrix. Which variable leaves the basis?
options: $x_1$ leaves
$x_6$ leaves
$x_5$ leaves
None, the program is unbounded

questions.question: For $\max Z=3x_1+2x_2+x_3$ subject to $x_1+2x_2+x_3\leq5$, $2x_1+3x_2+4x_3\leq8$, $\boldsymbol{x}\geq\boldsymbol{0}$, with slacks $x_4,x_5$, the basis $(x_1,x_2)$ has $\boldsymbol{B}^{-1}=\begin{bmatrix}-3&2\\2&-1\end{bmatrix}$. With $\bar{c}_j=-c_j+\boldsymbol{c}_{\mathcal{B}}^{\top}\boldsymbol{B}^{-1}\boldsymbol{A}_j$ and the most-negative rule, what does step 2 give?
options: $x_3$ enters, with reduced cost $10$
$x_4$ enters, with reduced cost $-5$
$x_5$ enters, with reduced cost $-4$
Optimal, as $\bar{c}_3=10\geq0$

questions.question: At a basic feasible solution of $\max Z=\boldsymbol{c}^{\top}\boldsymbol{x}$, every nonbasic reduced cost $\bar{c}_j=-c_j+\boldsymbol{c}_{\mathcal{B}}^{\top}\boldsymbol{B}^{-1}\boldsymbol{A}_j$ is nonnegative, and the nonbasic $x_2$ has $\bar{c}_2=3$ and a column $\boldsymbol{B}^{-1}\boldsymbol{A}_2$ without positive entries. What does the revised simplex algorithm conclude?
options: The program is unbounded, since $x_2$ can rise without limit and stay feasible
The solution is optimal, with further optimal solutions along the ray where $x_2$ rises
No optimum exists, since the feasible region is unbounded in the direction of $x_2$
The solution is optimal, and the column of $x_2$ plays no role in this conclusion

questions.question: For $\max Z=\boldsymbol{c}^{\top}\boldsymbol{x}$ with reduced costs $\bar{c}_j=-c_j+\boldsymbol{c}_{\mathcal{B}}^{\top}\boldsymbol{B}^{-1}\boldsymbol{A}_j$, step 2 of the revised simplex algorithm lets the variable with the most negative $\bar{c}_j$ enter. Which statement about this choice is correct?
options: It gives the largest possible increase of $Z$ in this iteration, namely $-\bar{c}_{j^*}$
It is needed for correctness: another variable with $\bar{c}_j<0$ could make $Z$ decrease
Any variable with $\bar{c}_j<0$ could enter, and the most negative need not raise $Z$ most
It guarantees that the algorithm cannot cycle and so stops after finitely many steps

questions.question: For $\max Z=3x_1+5x_2+4x_3$ subject to $x_1+2x_2+x_3\leq8$, $2x_1+x_2+3x_3\leq9$, $\boldsymbol{x}\geq\boldsymbol{0}$, with slacks $x_4,x_5$, the basis $(x_2,x_5)$ has $\boldsymbol{B}^{-1}=\begin{bmatrix}\frac{1}{2}&0\\-\frac{1}{2}&1\end{bmatrix}$, $\boldsymbol{x}_{\mathcal{B}}=(4,5)^{\top}$ and $Z=20$. What is $Z$ after one iteration with the most-negative rule?

For $\max Z=2x_1+x_2$ subject to $x_1-2x_2\leq4$, $-x_1+x_2\leq2$, $\boldsymbol{x}\geq\boldsymbol{0}$, with slacks $x_3,x_4$, the basis $(x_1,x_4)$ has $\boldsymbol{B}^{-1}=\begin{bmatrix}1&0\\1&1\end{bmatrix}$, $\boldsymbol{x}_{\mathcal{B}}=(4,6)^{\top}$ and $Z=8$. What does the next iteration of the revised simplex algorithm conclude?
options: $x_2$ enters; $\boldsymbol{B}^{-1}\boldsymbol{A}_2=(-2,-1)^{\top}$ has no positive entry, so the program is unbounded
$x_2$ enters and $x_4$ leaves at ratio $6$, from the positive entry of $\boldsymbol{A}_2=(-2,1)^{\top}$
$x_3$ enters, its reduced cost $2$ being the only positive one, and then $x_1$ leaves
$x_2$ enters and $x_1$ leaves, since $4/2=2$ is the smallest ratio once signs are dropped
